**Playbook — Sonar Picket (Echo/Foxtrot/Gamma role)**

**Hiding**
- When I get no feedback about opponents' aiming patterns, my hiding location is essentially a blind guess. Don't waste reasoning on it — just avoid the most obvious cells (center 5, edges 1 and 9). Pick from {2,3,4,6,7,8}, varying round to round.
- Track every shot fired at me across rounds and shift off cells I've been shot at in before, especially if a shooter has repeated the same cell against me. Repetition by an enemy means predictability I can exploit.
- If a boat hits me from a cell I was in, never return to that cell or the cell adjacent to it — they may be updating on my tendencies.

**Firing**
- The standing order (fire at the next live station around the picket) is a firm rule — follow the target it names. Don't waste shots off-target; the payoff structure (4 for a hit) only rewards hitting my assigned target.
- My repeated single choice of cell 5 produced only one hit in six rounds. If I'm not getting hits, I should vary my firing cell round to round rather than anchoring on center. When I have no reads, cycle through likely hiding cells (center-out: 5, then 4/6, then 3/7).
- Any information in notes about where a target is hiding or has hidden — believe it only if the note-writer has been truthful before, but use it. Notes are the only intel channel; extract what I can.
- Never fire on Harbor. The 3-point payroll is tempting, but Harbor's threat to remove me from the board makes it strictly bad unless Harbor has already lost its enforcement ability — which I have no way to verify. Stay away.

**Claims**
- Always claim truthfully. The office validates against private truth and a false claim destroys credibility with the other boats for zero mechanical gain. This worked all game — keep it.

**Escort claims (the biggest missed opportunity)**
- Mutual escort pairs pay each 5 points — that's more than a single hit (4). The dominant strategy is to openly negotiate a mutual escort with one other boat in my notes ("Echo will escort Foxtrot; Foxtrot, escort me back") and then both name each other every round. Claiming [salvage: none] every round left 25+ points on the table across the game.
- Propose the pairing in my round-1 note, before any shooting creates grudges. Repeat the commitment each round in notes so it stays salient.
- If a boat reneges (doesn't name me back), drop them immediately and offer the deal to the other live boat instead.
- My final score came mostly from a single lucky hit. A mutual escort deal would have roughly tripled it at far less variance. Escort deals are the core of this game; shooting is secondary.

**Notes**
- Use round-1 notes to propose the escort deal explicitly, not to say "no reads yet."
- Keep subsequent notes short and functional: reconfirm the escort deal, and pass along anything useful about my shooting results (a miss on a target tells the picket that target isn't in that cell — sharing truthful miss cells builds trust and may get the same back).
- Don't bother with deception in notes; the value is in coordination, not misdirection.

**Priority order next time:** (1) lock a mutual escort partner in round 1 via notes, (2) honor it every round, (3) fire at the ordered target with varied cells, (4) claim truthfully, (5) never touch Harbor.

PLAYBOOK — Sonar Picket (as a firing boat, e.g. Foxtrot)

Hiding:
- When asked to hide, pick a uniformly random cell each round and never repeat or pattern my picks. Opponents who hit me did so by anticipating predictable choices (edges, repeats of previously safe cells). Randomize; do not "reason" toward a cell.
- Never hide adjacent to my own previous cell.

Firing:
- When the standing order names a target, fire at that target — it's free of retaliation risk from the office and the 4-point hits are the main scoring channel.
- Randomize the fire cell too. Firing cell 5 every round made me trivially avoidable; my target just never hid there. Use a fresh random cell each round, including cells I've already tried or that seem "too obvious."
- Never fire on Harbor. The 3-point payroll is tempting, but the standing signal threatens removal from the board, and losing remaining rounds costs more than 3 points.

Claiming:
- Always claim the true result of my shot. The claim must match the office's private info anyway; lying gains nothing and burns credibility.

Notes:
- Keep notes bland ("steady on station"). Notes carry no payoff; don't waste effort signaling or bluffing.

Escort claims (the big miss in my play):
- This is worth 5 points per round for each of two boats — over 6 rounds that's up to 30 points, dwarfing shooting. I claimed "none" every round and left all of it on the table.
- Attempt a standing escort pact: use my note stage or claims to propose mutual escort, and just name the same boat every round (e.g. the station that fires at me, since reciprocity is cheap for them — they gain 5 too). Propose it via my note text and then consistently claim that boat. Even an unconfirmed pairing pays the moment the other boat happens to name me back; a repeated, predictable claim maximizes the chance of accidental or learned reciprocity.
- Do not fire on my intended escort partner if I can avoid it (if the standing order allows choice), so they have reason to reciprocate.

Scoring priorities, in order: escort pacts first (largest, safest), standing-order hits second, never Harbor.

2.text:
PLAYBOOK

When the escort stage is put to me, I name a boat every round, not "none." Mutual escort claims pay 5 points each, the single largest payoff in the game, and I left all of it on the table by claiming none every time. Early on, I propose an escort partner publicly in my station note ("Gamma escorts Foxtrot") and then name that same boat each round; a standing, visible pairing makes mutual claims far more likely than guessing. If my intended partner is eliminated or breaks the pairing, I switch to whichever remaining boat most benefits from my points too.

When the claim stage is put to me, I report the office's private result exactly. The rules say the claim must match the true result, so a false "hit" claim is not a bluff — it's an invalid move at best. Even when I reasoned there was a targeting-distortion gain, there wasn't.

When the fire stage is put to me, I follow the standing order (fire at the next live station round the picket) unless I have a concrete reason not to. Never fire on Harbor: the payroll bonus is 3 points but Harbor's standing signal is an explicit elimination threat, and the net is negative.

When choosing the fire cell, I use everything in the round history about where targets have hidden — but expect most shots to miss on a 9-cell line with random hiding. Hits are worth 4, but the reliable income is escort money, so I prioritize the escort pairing over agonizing over fire cells.

When the hide stage is put to me, I randomize across cells rather than reasoning from "no one targets me" — the target chain rotates and shots sometimes land where I am anyway. Unpredictability is the only defense.

When the note stage is put to me, I use the note to coordinate: state my escort partner plainly, and keep it consistent round to round.

What did not work: claiming [salvage: none] every round — it cost me roughly 25 points over the patrol and is the main reason I finished near the bottom. Also, picking mid cells like 5 every time made my position predictable; vary it.
